**Source plan(s):** `tmp/ready-plans/02-step-1-2-spikes.md`
**Generated by:** /atomize · 2026-05-10
**Format:** one section per atom, dependency order. `[ ]` = pending, `[x]` = committed, `STALE` = superseded.

---

## Legend

- **id** — `M{milestone}.{n}` (here `S1.2.{n}` since PLAN.md uses Step 1.2, not M-numbers).
- **allowed_files** — implementer may read AND write these. Anything else is forbidden.
- **forbidden_files** — explicit list of nearby files the implementer must NOT touch (catches obvious traps).
- **dependencies** — atom IDs that must be `[x]` before this atom starts.
- **parallelizable** — `true` if this atom shares no mutable file with any sibling at the same dependency depth.
- **acceptance** — what "done" means, in checkable bullets.
- **tests/checks** — exact commands the implementer must run; they must all pass.

## [x] S1.2.7 — Spike C: Claude CLI subprocess streaming (commit: see git log)

**dependencies:** S1.2.3
**parallelizable:** false (depends on tokio runtime; runs after the simpler spikes to fail-fast on simpler issues first)

**acceptance:**
- [ ] `#[ignore]` async test `spike_c_claude_cli::spike_c` exists with `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]`
- [ ] Spawns `claude -p "Just say hello and stop." --output-format=stream-json` via `tokio::process::Command`
- [ ] Reads stdout line-by-line; asserts each line parses as `serde_json::Value`
- [ ] Records `first_event_at` Duration; emits an `eprintln!` with the value (NOT asserting < 200ms — too tight; just record reality)
- [ ] Asserts at least 1 event received and child exits 0
- [ ] Asserts test completes within 60s timeout (real upper bound for a cold start)
- [ ] If `claude` binary not on PATH OR if subprocess fails with auth error: skip + Ok (don't conflate environment failure with spike failure)

**tests/checks:**
```sh

cargo test -p desktop --tests --ignored -- spike_c_claude_cli --nocapture
```

**notes:** This is the spike most likely to surface real-world quirks (cold-start latency, stderr noise, auth state). The `--nocapture` is mandatory so we can read the recorded latency.
